title: What percentage of sports fans watch streaming? (Q4 2025)

facts.fact: Parks Associates and InterDigital survey (released August 2025) found about 70% of U.S. sports viewers watch via streaming platforms.
facts.quote: Approximately 70% of U.S. sports viewers now watch via streaming platforms, with 40% watching sports exclusively through streaming

facts.fact: Parks Associates and InterDigital survey found 40% of U.S. sports viewers watch sports exclusively through streaming.
facts.quote: with 40% watching sports exclusively through streaming and 30% using both streaming and traditional TV

facts.fact: Parks Associates and InterDigital survey found 30% of U.S. sports viewers use both streaming and traditional TV.
facts.quote: 30% using both streaming and traditional TV

facts.fact: A Performance Research study found 90% of sports fans use at least one streaming service to watch live games.
facts.quote: found that 90% of sports fans use at least one streaming service to watch live games

facts.fact: A Performance Research study found 45% of respondents reported increased streaming sports viewership compared to the prior year.
facts.quote: with 45% reporting increased streaming sports viewership compared to the prior year

facts.fact: Performance Research data shows 63% of Gen Z sports viewers increased their sports streaming time year over year.
facts.quote: Gen Z leads at 63% increasing their sports streaming time year over year

facts.fact: Performance Research data shows 56% of Millennial sports viewers increased their sports streaming time year over year.
facts.quote: followed by Millennials at 56%

facts.fact: Performance Research data shows 35% of Gen X sports viewers reported increased sports streaming.
facts.quote: with 35% of Gen X and 21% of Boomers reporting increased sports streaming

facts.fact: Performance Research data shows 21% of Boomer sports viewers reported increased sports streaming.
facts.quote: with 35% of Gen X and 21% of Boomers reporting increased sports streaming

facts.fact: Parks Associates research found 43% of U.S. internet households identify as sports viewers.
facts.quote: Among the 43% of U.S. internet households that identify as sports viewers

facts.fact: Parks Associates research found 19% of U.S. sports viewers are sports traditionalists who watch exclusively through broadcast, cable, or satellite.
facts.quote: only 19% remain "sports traditionalists" who watch exclusively through traditional broadcast, cable, or satellite

facts.fact: Parks Associates found 84% of sports viewers watch at least one live sports event per week.
facts.quote: 84% of sports viewers watch at least one live sports event per week

facts.fact: AP-NORC polling found about six in ten people who follow sports extremely or very closely use sports-only streaming platforms.
facts.quote: About six in ten people who follow sports "extremely" or "very" closely use sports-only streaming platforms

facts.fact: Nielsen data shows 67% of viewers aged 18-34 watch sports primarily via streaming or social clips.
facts.quote: Among viewers 18-34, 67% watch sports primarily via streaming or social clips.

facts.fact: Nielsen data shows 52% of viewers aged 35-49 prefer streaming over cable for sports.
facts.quote: The 35-49 age group shows 52% preferring streaming over cable.

facts.fact: Performance Research found Amazon Prime Video has 65% usage among sports streaming viewers.
facts.quote: Amazon Prime Video leads sports streaming at 65% usage among sports streaming viewers, according to Performance Research.

facts.fact: Performance Research found ESPN+ has 39% usage among sports streaming viewers.
facts.quote: ESPN+ follows at 39%

facts.fact: Performance Research found Peacock captures 37% of sports streaming viewers.
facts.quote: Peacock captures 37% of sports streaming viewers

facts.fact: Performance Research found Paramount+ reaches 32% of sports streaming viewers.
facts.quote: Paramount+ reaches 32%

facts.fact: Apple TV+ is used by 17% of sports streaming viewers.
facts.quote: Apple TV+ has carved out niche position at 17%

facts.fact: Parks Associates reports direct-to-consumer sports service viewers spend an average of $111 per month on all streaming subscriptions.
facts.quote: direct-to-consumer sports service viewers spend an average of $111 per month on all streaming subscriptions

facts.fact: Performance Research found 68% of sports fans report concern over streaming costs.
facts.quote: Performance Research found 68% of sports fans report concern over streaming costs

facts.fact: Performance Research found 73% of sports fans say they are looking to reduce streaming expenses in the next six months.
facts.quote: 73% say they are looking to reduce streaming expenses in the next six months

facts.fact: Performance Research found 48% of streaming sports fans feel more connected to their favorite teams and sports through streaming.
facts.quote: Performance Research found 48% of streaming sports fans feel more connected to their favorite teams and sports through streaming

facts.fact: InterDigital research found 40% of sports viewers under 35 watch sports on social media platforms, compared with 13% of those 55 and older.
facts.quote: InterDigital research found 40% of sports viewers under 35 watch sports on social media platforms, compared to just 13% of those 55 and older.

facts.fact: About 40% of sports fans use sports-only direct-to-consumer services such as ESPN+, MLB TV, NFL Sunday Ticket, or NBA League Pass, rising to 60% among super fans.
facts.quote: About 40% of sports fans use platforms like ESPN+, MLB TV, NFL Sunday Ticket, or NBA League Pass, with that figure rising to 60% among super fans
